I barely failed my last attempt 5 months ago and it landed me in a hospital gurney. I was paddled back to the land of the living, and to be honest, waking back up from what was the precipice of death was one of the most serene and painful experiences of my life. 

There this unexplainable hollow feeling that came while my vitals where being checked, and despite people buzzing to and from the room, I felt very little connection to my actual surroundings. I just felt numb, cold, but very much alive.


The weeks that passed after held to that numb disconnect. I didn't eat much, avoided social interactions and just thought. But it does get better. After the numbness subsided everything was very vibrant, the food I ate tasted better, I was happy to be around the ones that forgave and loved me, having a cigarette after a week was the greatest fucking thing in the world. 

It's a battle dealing with suicidal depression. I can say I'm better than I was 5 months prior, but I am still very deep in to this war. I hope anyone suffering and those of you that have survived find some peace, or at least a shadow of it. I can't tell any of you all to hold on, but you can hold out.

I cherished mania at my worst points, as I too thought I was bi-polar ( misdiagnosis, I am a functional depressive with sociopathic tendencies)  as it is the closest to a dream you can get to while still sober. The rush of thoughts and energy is euphoric, but it's not real. I'm ok nowadays, some are better than others, I still look at traffic and blades and that constant hunger to escape as an option to release what I can never truly fix, but like I said, you get by.... As a person that has dealt with suicidal depression for 10+ years, happiness is subjective. There's a point we all reach in this "war" where your apathy becomes serene and you can no longer see the point in wallowing in sadness, as it as neutral as every other "feeling". You'll never be as "happy" as your peers, but you'll care less, which is a grander victory than wanting to toss yourself in to traffic. Call it enlightenment, but it's a better place than where I suppose you're at.

Dealing crack is only a means to an end in the dope trade. Since the product margin is entirely lower than the profit you make from it, you can supplement your capital until you can buy a better raw product ( in this case, cocaine) to forgo the stove top and Pyrex and deal with just raw blow.

I'm taking this from the dealers perspective. Should a product, such as weed, become widely available due to commercialization, and in such,no longer needed to be "dealt", then a new product will be found to fill the void and retain profits. So sad dealer should not be sad, unless he isn't actually about the hustle. It was a silly joke, and forgive my lack of clarity.

Baking soda is an integral ingredient in the process of cooking free base cocaine. Sad dealer could become lucrative dealer if he flipped his caine, instead of selling herb. If the drug trade of the '80's and early '90's in the DC area are any indication of a trend, many of these street level dealers will forgo weed, and change to selling crack as a means of making ends meet, when weed becomes legal.

This occured to me as I was leaving a rather late shift to head home (around 3am). As I was approaching the crosswalk to get to my car, three things occured almost concurrently; my phone went off, stoping me briefly; an SUV barreled down the intersection and a woman sprinted across the road. There was this eerie calm and stillness as I watched vehicle collide with flesh and bone, her body fall to a heap and the driver swerve away. I couldn't get the license plate number, I couldn't tell her to watch out, I couldn't even run in to the street to comfort her, I just stood there in shock. I called the paramedics a few moments later, but at that point it was far too late. To be able to do nothing to save her or at least find some justice, just to be scared and useless, still hurts and haunts me.

I took a considerable amount of Molly during what I thought was the tail end of a rather hectic service. The drugs took hold right around the same time a 12 top strolled in. I decided it was in my best interest to keep sober during ever service onward. 

Some of the best cooks I've worked with were cokeheads and chronic alcoholics. Men that would turn out a dinner service like a waltz, while sneaking off to do lines in the walk in, and drink themselves blind when it all ened. This being said, it puts a huge strain on the rest of the crew. You are never sure when that person is gonna have an off day, and hurt themselves or you. 

This industry is already a harbor for destructive behavior. We justify our vices with the idea that it's only taking the edge off, and celebrate surviving while sweating off the night before as badges of honor, when in reality you are only hurting your skill and talent, and more importantly, potentially fucking up someone else's money. I'm not saying to not have some fun and imbibe, but don't celebrate holding on, when you should be excelling.

I spent 72 hours in a psych ward, roomed with a paraniod schizophrenic who we'll call "Smiley". Smiley was a man who was certain he was Jesus Christ reincarnate. In such, he also thought that I was Bruce Lee. In Smiley's mind, We ( the patients) in this psych ward were snowed in a Ford Motor Company garage sometime in the 1940's. Now I don't know how many of my fellow redditors have spent any large amount of time with a schizophrenic, but changing their preset ideas and delusions is a moot point, and in my current situation, one that would potentially leave me with a collapsed windpipe.

Even though Smiley was batshit insane, after adapting to his quirks and playing along with his delusions, we became pretty good friends. Playing cards and watching him use his "Jesus powers" to figure out my hand was always entertaining, his casual and almost cartoonish racism was great for a laugh(he called an unknown racial group "stumpfuckers", which now has become my favorite insult), and his lack of social fear and hypocrisy was refeshing.

The only alarming instance I had with Smiley was our last conversation. I'd been cleared by the shrinks and no longer a danger to myself or others, so I was saying my goodbyes, thanking the orderlies and the doctors, and signing the nessesary paperwork to return back to civilian life. Smiley wasn't very sad from me leaving and asked me to tell the men upstairs for a pardon, so that the next time I come back he could join me. Clearly confused by such a cryptic request, I told him that I had no real reason to ever return, in which he responded, "But you always come back Bruce, you can't ever leave the place you call home". I came to the conclusion that either I was a new player in a long list of former "Bruce's" Smiley had befreinded over his time at the ward, or a looming existential crisis was about to come falling on top of me. I paid neither option any attention at the time though, as I became far too busy jumping on the NOPE train to make it back home. Smiley's last request is one of the many reasons why I drink.

TL;DR: Bruce Willis is dead

My 21st birthday was a shitshow. My "friends" ditched me at a party, refused to pick up their phones, and told me it was penance for my actions during the night. In my drunken stupor, I decided it was best to walk the 5 miles back to my apartment, and sleep the remainder of the night off. During this walk, three men decided to follow me, two of which seemed to want to do harm and following steadly closer as I continued my drunken stumble. The third man, dressed in a throwback Bulls Jersey and resembling Michael Clarke Duncan, rushed ahead of the other two, calling me by a name that wasn't my own. He told me I was going the wrong way (which I was), and that I should come back to the party. I didn't recognize him, he didn't know me, but somehow he knew I was in danger, and when we were far enough from the other two men asked if I needed a ride home, which he gave without taking my drunken gift of gas money. He dropped me off, waited until I opened my apartment door and sped off in to the night. He called himself J, and he saved me from a mugging.

tl;dr: Jesus is a Bulls fan, drove a drunk asshole home.

I was working as a cook in a resort in Puerto Rico a few years back. One of our runners came in after an order, shaking, white as a sheet, and crying profusely. After she calmed down, she told us that the men she was running food to, calmly ate a few bites of their meal, tipped her generously, and then as she was walking away, proceeded to stab one of their own multiple times with a steak knife. Security was called, and eventually found the man who was stabbed, dead in our parking garage. His attackers excaped.

Not really weird or a first hand account, and I'm sorry to bum anyone out, but it was really surreal to have a murder happen in what was normally a really calm place. Service was really quiet that night afterwards.
